issue.title: Syntax as routing: E_b-conditioned infill step consuming forward anchors (#393 §5)
issue.body:
## Motivation (program: #393 §5; criterion: #394)

Day-0 measurement (#394, PR #396): a table conditioned on nothing but (next anchor token, distance) hits **32.7% top-1 at offset 3** — statistically tied with the entire shipped causal store at that position — while the architecture consumes zero forward context. The offset gradient (14.2 → 19.0 → 32.7) is syntactic anticipation. This issue designs and measures the mechanism that consumes it.

## Design obligation

An inference step that, given the pinned anchors of the infill task, routes **backward from the next anchor** through reverse indexes (E_b) while routing forward through transition edges (E_f), scoring free positions from the intersection — grammar as precompiled routing structure, the R4-native counterpart of attention's content-based lookback. The format already carries E_f/E_b (Theorem 7 canonical edge IDs); what does not exist is a serving step that reads E_b conditioned on a *future* token.

## Measurement ladder (all on the #394 harness; certifier-side until proven)

1. **Headroom probe (cheap, first):** fuse the existing causal store with the fwd-anchor table (backoff and score-fusion variants) — pure instrumentation upper bound on what any forward-consuming mechanism can add. If fusion does not beat 34.7% overall, stop and rethink.
2. **E_b-conditioned arm:** replace the raw fwd-anchor table with backward routing from the next anchor's region(s) through E_b, intersected with the causal frontier.
3. **Gates (#393 table):** clear the fwd-anchor null at off3 (≥32.7%), then clear the shipped store overall (≥34.7%), on held-out; #391 null discipline throughout.

## Non-goals

No serving-path or schema changes until gate 2 passes; no scoring-term additions to the open next-token rows (measured dead end per #393).

comments.body:
## Gate 1: PASSED — fusion probes (harness extension in PR #401)

Same fixture protocol as the #394 Day-0 table (500k records, held-out free targets 75,385). Three instrumentation fusions of the causal store with the trivial (next-anchor-token, distance) count table:

| arm | top1 (free) | off1 | off2 | off3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| shipped causal store | 34.7% | 34.5 | 34.8 | 35.0 |
| fuse: offset-route | 34.1% | 34.5 | 34.8 | 33.0 |
| fuse: count-confidence | 37.5% | 34.5 | 35.7 | 42.3 |
| **fuse: product-of-experts** | **43.4%** | **37.9** | **41.9** | **50.5** |

Findings:

1. **Naive replacement loses; composition wins.** Swapping the fwd table in at off3 (offset-route) is net negative, but multiplying the two smoothed distributions gains at *every* offset — the forward-anchor signal is largely independent of the causal signal, which is exactly what makes a consuming mechanism worth building.
2. **+8.7pp absolute over the shipped store** on the infill slice, and above the all-time-best open-row config (41.00%, #374 rows-emit) — from one token of forward context and a count table. Half of off3 positions become predictable (50.5%).
3. Even off1 — three tokens ahead of the anchor — gains +3.4pp from composition.

Ladder step 2 (E_b-conditioned arm: backward routing from the next anchor's regions intersected with the causal frontier) is now unlocked and justified. The 43.4% product fusion is the instrumentation bound that arm should approach; the off3 50.5% is its target position.

Caveats: instrumentation fusion is not a serving mechanism (f32, allocation, table lookups outside the contract); fixture distribution; single stride; natural-corpus rerun pending #381.

## Step 2, measurement A: region-conditioned forward tables (fixture)

Keyed the forward table by the anchor token's **graded-code prefix** (its compiled geometric address, `token_codes`) at every depth, instead of raw token identity:

| arm | top1 (free) | off1 | off2 | off3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| null: fwd-region-d1 | 7.6% | 6.8 | 7.3 | 8.6 |
| null: fwd-region-d2 | 18.5% | 12.5 | 15.9 | 27.1 |
| null: fwd-region-d3 | 21.8% | 14.1 | 18.9 | 32.3 |
| null: fwd-region-d4 | 21.9% | 14.2 | 19.0 | 32.6 |
| null: fwd-anchor-table (token id) | 21.9% | 14.2 | 19.0 | 32.7 |
| fuse: product-region | 43.4% | 38.0 | 41.9 | 50.5 |
| fuse: product (token) | 43.4% | 37.9 | 41.9 | 50.5 |

Reading, both directions stated honestly:

1. **The geometric address is a sufficient statistic for the anchor's syntax influence at this density**: d3 (3 bytes) reproduces the token-identity table to within 0.1pp everywhere, and fusion is identical. Nothing about the anchor's syntactic pull on its neighborhood is lost by addressing it geometrically.
2. **The generalization question is starved, not answered**: only 2.1% of held-out (distance, anchor-token) keys are unseen on the fixture (1,579/75,385), so region-bucketing has no sparsity to rescue. Region-vs-token can only separate where the token table fails — that regime is the natural corpus (#381 obs, larger effective vocabulary, thinner per-anchor counts) and larger strides. The natural-corpus rerun is the discriminating experiment and stays queued behind #381.

Next per ladder: step-2 measurement B on natural corpus once /tmp/wiki-obs finalizes; then the serving-shape question (an E_b walk from anchor regions rather than a certifier table).

## Ari's question answered: the forward channel survives trigram rows (PR #405)

Question on the record: do the fusion numbers include NGRAM (trigram) rows? They did not — so we added the rows-inclusive baseline (certifier-side trigram proxy: exact (prev₂, prev₁) → next table from the construction partition, argmax-when-resolved, same semantics as the NGR1 rows the 41.0% config used):

| arm | top1 (free) | off1 | off2 | off3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| null: trigram alone | 34.7% | 33.7 | 35.3 | 35.2 |
| rows-proxy: tri → store backoff | 36.0% | 35.8 | 36.2 | 35.9 |
| fuse: store × tri (causal best) | 36.4% | 36.3 | 36.3 | 36.5 |
| **fuse: store × tri × fwd** | **43.6%** | **39.2** | **42.5** | **49.3** |

**The forward-anchor channel adds +7.2pp over the trigram-inclusive causal baseline.** Trigrams and the forward channel are mechanistically disjoint — exact backward context vs forward anchor — and the three-way product shows they are informationally near-disjoint too: the fwd gain over store-only was +8.7pp, over store×tri it is still +7.2pp. Trigrams absorb ~1.5pp of the forward signal, no more.

Bits ladder (#394 gate item, same run): unigram 8.660 | store 8.453 | fwd-table alone 11.276 | **product 6.803 bits/token** — fusion is −1.65 bits vs the store. (The fwd table alone is bits-poor because its smoothed mass is thin off the pre-anchor offsets; composition is where it pays.)

Caveats: certifier-side trigram proxy (table, not the serving NGR1 emission path); fixture distribution; natural-corpus rerun queued behind #381.

Natural-corpus interim for the #399 threads (full table on #394): (1) the fusion story does NOT transfer as measured — no token-granular channel, forward-anchor included, beats the unigram null on wiki text at 534k training positions; the stories-measured anticipation signal is distribution-dependent. (2) The step-2 decider finally has sparsity: region-conditioning beats token identity under 17% key-miss (fwd-region-d1 4.5% vs token 4.1%) — direction confirmed at frequency level. Both verdicts need the naturally-compiled-artifacts rerun before they're final; that run is the queued decider.

## M0 (E_b-mediated region walk) — first full verdict, both regimes (full tables on #394)

Per the resolved design forks (region-code unit, distance-tagged tables, fused frontier):

| regime | m0 alone | token fwd-table | m0 fusion | token fusion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fixture (dense) | 19.9% | 21.9% | 37.9% | **43.6%** |
| natural (sparse) | 4.1% | 4.1% | 2.5% | 1.9% |

**Exit rule (within ~2pp of the 43.6% bound): MISSED — 5.7pp short.** Where token keys are dense, the top-8 emitting-region mixture blurs what exact identity resolves. Under natural sparsity M0 reaches parity and fuses better. Sharpest diagnostic: at d1 region granularity on fixture, M0 routes BELOW the frequency null (54.4% vs 61.2%) while trigram is +7 above it — the mixture actively mis-routes neighborhoods.

Design consequence for step 3: the walk needs **confidence gating, not just backoff** — token-key conditioning when the key is seen (dense regime), region mediation only where keys are sparse, and region-mixture width shrunk or score-weighted (top-8 uniform-ish mixing is the mis-routing mechanism). Same hybrid shape step 2 converged to.

Bigger context that bounds this work (full record on #394): on natural text at 534k positions NO channel — causal, forward, geometric, tabular, or fused — beats the unigram floor at any granularity; only EXCT verbatim matching does (36.5%). The forward-anchor channel that motivated this issue is real on the story distribution and absent on encyclopedic text at this scale. #399's mechanism work should therefore target the **substrate direction** (E_f/E_b over observed exact-context structure — the score-pipeline world, where the 36.5% lives) and/or wait on the **scale** question. Design session with Casey continues.

## Re-scope (recorded per the 08-04 findings; issue stays open as the mechanism track)

The founding premise — a token-granular forward-anchor channel — measured real on the story fixture (+7.2pp over rows-inclusive causal) and null on natural text at 534k positions (scoped: may reopen at scale). M0 (region-mediated E_b walk) recorded parity under sparsity, a 5.7pp dense-regime cost, and d1 neighborhood mis-routing — design law: confidence-gated hybrid, narrow score-weighted mixtures.

**New scope, per the substrate resolution on #393:** the E_b mechanism now targets the stack that measurably works on natural text — the score compiler's induced-cover store (36.5% vs the legacy floor). Concretely: (1) forward/anticipatory conditioning as an operator over induced-cover regions (the E_f/E_b edges of the graph stack, where they natively live), graded by the in-tree infill harness against induced-cover baselines; (2) the icosian toolchain (#395 record: storage/distances/arithmetic all contract-native) as the representation for those regions; (3) the confidence-gated hybrid shape from M0's record. Retest of the token-granular channel rides the scale track (10k corpus in observation).

## M1 design (substrate scope): forward-anchor conditioning over the INDUCED cover — implementable with existing pub APIs

Read of the working substrate (`uor_r4_graph_compiler::induction`): the score compiler's cover = hierarchical spherical k-means over the same centered context bundles the harness already computes; regions carry depth/parent/children + per-region next-token counts + entropy; per-observation top-1 region PATHS are returned; transition edges between regions (CoverEdge kind 2) are the native E_f, reversible into E_b by canonical sort.

**M1 arms (one harness test, natural corpus, D3 split):**
1. `induce_cover` over construction bundles (config matching the score run's budget) → per-position region paths — this reproduces the 36.5% substrate INSIDE the harness protocol (its own validation row: region-path-keyed store with observed evidence).
2. **Forward channel over induced regions:** (distance d, anchor's region path prefix) → target-token table, built from construction; at eval the anchor's region comes from the emission inversion (which regions emit the anchor token), top-k weighted — the confidence-gated hybrid per the M0 record (token-key when the anchor token is region-unambiguous, region mixture only when needed, mixture width scored not uniform).
3. Fusion with the causal region-path store per the measured composition law.

Exit rules: arm 1 within ~2pp of the score pipeline's 36.5% (protocol-parity check); arm 2/3 graded against the arm-1 causal baseline — ANY reproducible gain over it on natural text is the first forward-context win outside the fixture, i.e. the mechanism this issue was filed for, on the substrate that works. Implementation starting now; compute ~30 min/run behind the scale loop.

## M1 result: exit rule 1 FAILED — for a protocol reason that redirects the work productively

Run (natural corpus, D3 split, in-tree harness): default CoverConfig induced only **16 regions / depth 3** — orders of magnitude coarser than the working substrate — so induced-causal landed at the unigram floor (4.5%/4.6%) and the forward/fusion arms had nothing to condition on (4.3%). The harness-protocol reproduction of the 36.5% is NOT achieved, and the deeper trace explains why reproduction is the wrong strategy: the score pipeline's Rule 1 (graph chain, chain-telescoped scoring over regions + edges, no EXCT) alone posts 26.9% on the same held-out — the mechanism is the composed chain scorer, not a flat region-path store, and its EXCT section is built from a TLS1 store with compile-time residualized scoring against the root prior. Flat-key reproductions structurally miss it.

**M2 (next, replacing harness reproduction):** implement the forward-anchor channel INSIDE the score pipeline — an anchor-conditioned term in `GraphScorer::score_candidates` (or a parallel instrumentation row in `score_command`), using the pipeline's own regions/edges/eval — graded by the same certified protocol that produces the 36.5%/26.9% rows, with win/loss instrumentation against Rule 1+2. Serving-native from the first measurement; no protocol-parity gap possible. M1 harness ships for the record (it is the honest negative + the config diagnosis).

Records for 2026-08-04 (all on natural wiki-obs, 100,306 held-out, Gate C instrumentation; PRs #414/#415/#416/#417):

**M2 (true anchor, = A-mode):** fused 39.6%/7.9222 vs Rule 1+2 36.5%/8.3534; live 40.9 vs 36.7 (+4.2pp, n=73,806); first config to beat TLA3 baseline (39.1%) in-pipeline.
**B′ (self-anchor, teacher-forced ctx):** self 39.8 (live 41.2 vs 36.6); GATED self 40.0 (live 45.0 vs 39.4, 2.10:1); anchor-hat accuracy 32.5% — lift retained despite wrong anchors (representative-not-correct mechanism).
**Falsifier 1 (draft drift, real two-pass):** DRAFT-gated 35.9/9.3847; live 40.4 vs 41.3 — NEGATIVE (+966/−1,581). Naive standalone two-pass REFUTED; B′ result was conditional on true intermediate context.

**Scoreboard:** A-mode infill serving VALIDATED (drift-immune, anchors are inputs; FWDA section + score_candidates_infill shipped in #416). Naive B refuted (#417 record). Rescues (strict per-step gate, iterative re-draft, beam) unmeasured — strict-gate arm queued tonight. Falsifier 2 (coverage-vs-consistency) runs at scale on the wiki10k corpus.

Falsifier-2 scale campaign record (10k wiki corpus, 2,110,111 records, κ f19c1494; POST-#407 era; PRs pending merge carry the harness/env work):

**All three phases NEGATIVE at scale — and the diagnosis converts the result from a channel verdict into a substrate capacity finding.**
Score gate C (402,802 held-out): Rule 1+2 26.1%/22.13 bits (vs 36.5%/8.35 at 500k) | true-anchor fused 16.2% (INVERTED, −9.9pp) | all anchored arms ≤ base | anchor-hat accuracy 0.1% | ExactContext 97.8%.
Harness (2.1M): shipped-store 0.3% | product 2.4% | store×tri×fwd 2.7% (vs 34.9/43.2/43.5 on fixture).
M-R2: router 3.9% vs unigram 4.0% vs shuffled 3.7% — NEGATIVE.

**Capacity diagnosis (Casey's hypothesis, confirmed in code):** every capacity knob is constant while data grew 4.2×. Cover ANTI-scaled (15 nodes vs 39): split acceptance uses an ABSOLUTE 0.25-bit entropy-gain floor that broad heterogeneous regions can't clear. Real RVQ k-means cap is 10,000 samples (log's '100000' is a progress-bar total). Emission entries = 64×regions → 896 vs 2,432. FWDA truncation loses growing mass at fixed cap 64.

**Decisive experiments running:** M-C1 (500k story-boundary subsample of the SAME corpus, all defaults — dilution control) and M-C2 (full corpus, ratio-scaled knobs: CTX_SAMPLE 211k, RVQ 42k, cover K0 34, caps 270 — capacity arm). Knobs are env-overridable and κ-neutral-unset (PR #432, kappa_reproduction verified bit-identical). Interpretation rules pre-declared: M-C1 recovery → dilution confirmed; M-C2 recovery → capacity-scaling law established and the fwd-channel verdict REOPENS at proper capacity; neither recovers → corpus-difficulty explanation gains ground and the 500k positives stand as regime-scoped records.

M-C1 verdict: DILUTION REFUTED. The 499,985-record story-boundary subsample of the wiki10k corpus, at identical capacity and defaults, scores Rule 1+2 26.0%/20.42 bits — statistically identical to the full 2.1M run (26.1%) and nowhere near the original 500k corpus (36.5%). Fwd channel inverted here too (18.2% all / live 14.0 vs 26.4). Also: Rule 1 alone (27.1%) beats Rule 1+2 (26.0%) on this corpus — EXCT precedence slightly negative under high topic diversity. **The decisive variable is corpus composition (≈600 deeply-observed articles vs 10,000 broad topics), not scale and not capacity dilution.** All 36.5-era records — including the A-mode +4.2pp — are hereby scoped to redundancy-rich corpora. M-C2 (capacity-scaled compile on full 2.1M) still running; its question is now how much scaled capacity claws back on a genuinely broad corpus (cover trajectory 39→21→15 says the entropy-floor mechanism is real but secondary).

M-C2 verdict (full 2.1M corpus, ratio-scaled capacity: CTX_SAMPLE 211k, RVQ 42k, cover K0 34, caps 270): **capacity scaling works structurally but claws back almost nothing on quality.** Cover 69 nodes (vs 15 starved — 4.6×, the entropy-floor fix is real), emission entries 4,352 (vs 896). But Rule 1+2 only 26.5% (vs 26.1 starved, 26.0 subsample); Rule 1 27.1% unchanged; fwd channel still inverted (16.5% all, live 11.5 vs 26.9). **Consolidated falsifier-2 conclusion: corpus composition dominates. The substrate scores ~26-27% on broad-topic corpora at every measured capacity; the 36.5-era numbers (and the A-mode +4.2pp, the M-R1/B2 router positives) are records of the redundancy-rich regime. EXCT precedence is mildly negative under diversity (R1 > R1+2 on both wiki10k runs). The fwd channel inverts on broad corpora regardless of capacity.** Falsifier-2 record complete.

Closing with the complete record (Casey, 2026-08-05). The program delivered: A-mode infill serving validated and shipped for the redundancy-rich regime (+4.2pp live; FWDA section, score_candidates_infill, infill_fill, graph infill CLI — PRs #414-#419); standalone two-pass refuted (2 falsifications); falsifier-2 resolved — corpus composition dominates (M-C1 dilution refuted, M-C2 capacity claws back +0.4pp with a 4.6× healthier cover), all regime scopes recorded; capacity knobs env-overridable κ-neutrally (#432); cover entropy-floor and RVQ-cap mechanisms located. Successor: broad-corpus frontier issue (filed above). Shipped surfaces remain valid for their measured regime.
